extracted.intended_audience: readers, potential contributors, advertisers, press, and job applicants seeking information about The Onion
extracted.subtask_short: The Onion submission and contact policies
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational policies and procedural guidelines for contacting The Onion, submitting material (and the prohibition on submissions), advertising/licensing inquiries, technical support, and staff/career/contact practices for this satirical news publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: No outside submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No, The Onion does not accept outside submissions of any kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Onion will not respond to any unsolicited submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsolicited résumés not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not send résumés unless specifically told to do so in a job listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any unsolicited résumés will be immediately discarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careers posting procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Onion Inc. regularly posts new openings on the Careers section of our website; editorial openings will be posted there on the exceedingly rare occasions they occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only apply through listed job postings; do not send unsolicited applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsolicited bulk email policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Unsolicited bulk email, email attachments, and junk email of any kind are not accepted, and will be filtered and immediately discarded upon receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical issue reporting procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: To report a technical issue with TheOnion.com, submit a request through the Kinja support center with a summary of the issue and your browser information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include browser information and a summary to help diagnostics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising inquiry procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send all advertising inquiries to advertising@theonion.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the business you would like to advertise; the appropriate advertising sales representative will get back to you promptly. For more information regarding advertising opportunities, consult the Media Kit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press and events contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send press and events inquiries to press@theonion.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also use press@theonion.com for requests to cover The Onion and for speaking engagement inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback on articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send all concerns about an Onion article to publicfeedback@theonion.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Onion cannot guarantee a response to any feedback to its content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions / reprint policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Onion may not be reprinted or retransmitted in whole or in part without the express written consent of the publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To license material from The Onion, send a request to permissions@theonion.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archive requests and access
rubrics_metrics.description: This website contains all of The Onion's articles published from early 1996 through the present and can be browsed or searched online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For requests for articles and graphics from past issues, including those published before 1996, send requests to archive@theonion.com. The Onion will attempt to answer but cannot guarantee a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaking engagements availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The writers and editors of America’s Finest News Source and its sister sites are available for speaking engagements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send inquiries about speaking engagements to press@theonion.com; examples of venues include universities, conferences, and festivals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name usage in stories
rubrics_metrics.description: The Onion uses invented names in all of its stories, except in cases where public figures are being satirized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other use of real names is accidental and coincidental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal stance on satire and lawsuits
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not sue The Onion; The First Amendment protects satire as a form of free speech and expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is cited as the publication's legal/ethical stance regarding satirical content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age guidance for readership
rubrics_metrics.description: The Onion is not intended for readers under 18 years of age.
